children: South Korean carmakers' competitive resilience against Chinese rivals may not last as the global market shifts toward electric vehicles, says Capital Economics' Gareth Leather. Chinese brands accounted for 44% of EV sales in Korea in the first nine months of this year, up from 34% in 2025 and just 5% in 2022, the economist notes. Overseas, South Korean manufacturers also risk losing ground to Chinese rivals, which have a greater advantage in battery technology, production scale and costs, Leather says. Hyundai and Kia's success in hybrid vehicles has helped offset weaker performance in EVs, but this may offer only temporary protection if the transition to EVs gathers pace, he adds. (kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)
